objective: Replace the visually fixed enclosed base with a connected four-module steer-drive chassis that clearly supports autonomous forward, lateral, diagonal, and rotate-in-place motion while retaining retractable stabilizers for manipulation.
acceptance: the base has four independent steer-drive modules with visible connected wheel, fork, steering bearing, and chassis load paths
the declared motion modes include longitudinal, lateral, diagonal, and rotate-in-place movement
stabilizers are retracted during navigation and deploy only for stationary manipulation
SCAD, STEP, engineering drawings, interactive render, campaign image, BOM, and assembly sequence agree on the holonomic base
autonomous navigation software and physical drive validation remain explicitly incomplete
mechanical tests, Ruff, and Task Packet validation pass
stop_conditions: the chassis change requires inventing finished navigation, motor-control, localization, or safety performance
wheel modules cannot maintain guarded steering hardware and a connected structural path
the base would lose the brake and stabilizer requirements needed for dual-arm manipulation
the visual would imply physical drive validation that has not occurred
